questions.stem: What is the primary function of the epidermis in plants?
questions.solution: The epidermis is the outermost layer of the plant body and is covered with a waxy cuticle that prevents water loss. This makes it the primary function of the epidermis. The other options describe functions of different parts of the plant, such as the xylem for water transport, the mesophyll for photosynthesis, and the vascular bundles for support.

hi.stem: पौधों में एपिडर्मिस का प्राथमिक कार्य क्या है?

hi.solution: एपिडर्मिस पौधे के शरीर की सबसे बाहरी परत होती है और जल हानि को रोकने के लिए एक मोम की परत से ढकी रहती है। इस कारण एपिडर्मिस का प्राथमिक कार्य जल हानि को रोकना होता है। अन्य विकल्प पौधे के अन्य भागों, जैसे जाइलम के जल परिवहन, मेसोफिल के प्रकाश संश्लेषण और जाइलम एवं फ्लोएम के लिए समर्थन के कार्य का वर्णन करते हैं।

mr.stem: वनस्पतीमध्ये एपिडर्मिसचे प्राथमिक कार्य काय आहे?
mr.solution: एपिडर्मिस हे वनस्पतीच्या शरीराचे बाह्यतम पर्पटी असून त्यावर एक वैयक्तिक कटिल असते जे पाणी गमावणे टाळते. हे एपिडर्मिसचे प्राथमिक कार्य बनते. इतर विकल्पांमध्ये वनस्पतीच्या विविध भागांचे कार्य वर्णन केले आहे, उदाहरणार्थ, पाणी वहावे यासाठी जाइलेम, प्रकाशसंश्लेषणासाठी मेसोफिल आणि समर्थनासाठी वास्क्युलर बंडल्स.

questions.stem: What is the main function of the cuticle on the epidermis of plant leaves?
choices: To allow the entry of carbon dioxide
To absorb water and minerals from the soil
To prevent the loss of water
To allow the entry of oxygen
questions.solution: The cuticle is a waxy layer on the epidermis that prevents water loss. Root hairs absorb water and minerals, not the cuticle. The cuticle does not allow carbon dioxide entry, as that happens through stomata. Structural support is provided by other tissues like collenchyma and sclerenchyma.

hi.stem: पौधों के पत्तियों के एपिडर्मिस पर क्यूटिकल का मुख्य कार्य क्या है?

questions.stem: What is the role of trichomes in the epidermis of stems?
choices: To help in the process of transpiration
questions.solution: Trichomes help in preventing water loss by reducing the rate of transpiration. They are not involved in water absorption, which is done by root hairs. They do not provide structural support, which is done by other tissues.

questions.stem: If a transverse section of a plant stem shows vascular bundles that are scattered and surrounded by sclerenchymatous tissue, what type of stem is it likely to be?

questions.stem: In a transverse section of a monocot stem, how are the vascular bundles arranged compared to a dicot stem?
questions.solution: In a monocot stem, the vascular bundles are scattered throughout the ground tissue, unlike in a dicot stem where they are arranged in a ring. questions.stem: In a dorsiventral leaf, which part of the mesophyll consists of elongated cells arranged vertically and parallel to each other?
questions.solution: In a dorsiventral leaf, the palisade parenchyma consists of elongated cells arranged vertically and parallel to each other. The spongy parenchyma is loosely arranged, the cortex is part of the root, and the endodermis is a layer in the root, not the leaf. The palisade parenchyma is specifically adapted for photosynthesis.

questions.stem: A researcher observes that in a flowering plant, the stamens mature before the pistil. What is the most likely effect of this timing difference?
questions.solution: If the stamens mature before the pistil, it ensures cross-pollination. This is because the pollen is available before the stigma is receptive, reducing the chances of self-pollination. Autogamy and geitonogamy involve self-pollination, while cross-pollination is the most likely outcome in this scenario. Hence, the correct answer is that it ensures cross-pollination.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the epidermal cells in the root?

questions.stem: Which part of the stem provides mechanical strength to the young stem?

questions.stem: If a flower has a tricarpellary syncarpous ovary, which of the following is most likely true?
choices: The flower has three separate carpels

questions.stem: A plant has a leaf with stomata on both surfaces and undifferentiated mesophyll. What type of leaf is it most likely to be?
questions.solution: An isobilateral leaf has stomata on both surfaces and undifferentiated mesophyll, which matches the description. Dorsiventral leaves typically have stomata only on the lower surface and differentiated mesophyll. Monocot leaves usually have a different structure, and dicot leaves generally have a different mesophyll arrangement.

questions.stem: Why are the guard cells in grasses described as dumb-bell shaped?

questions.stem: Why do monocot roots not undergo secondary growth?
choices: Because they have a large pith
Because they lack a cambium layer
Because they have more xylem bundles
Because they have a sclerenchymatous hypodermis
questions.solution: The correct answer is because they lack a cambium layer, as secondary growth requires a cambium to produce additional vascular tissues. Monocots do not have this layer, preventing secondary growth. The other options are incorrect because a large pith, more xylem bundles, or a sclerenchymatous hypodermis do not directly affect the ability to undergo secondary growth.

questions.stem: Why is the pith in a monocot root more developed than in a dicot root?
choices: Because monocot roots undergo secondary growth
Because monocot roots have more vascular bundles
Because monocot roots have a larger number of xylem bundles
Because monocot roots have a larger number of endodermal cells
questions.solution: The correct option is because monocot roots have more vascular bundles. This is because the increased number of vascular bundles contributes to the development of a larger pith. The other options are incorrect because monocot roots do not undergo secondary growth, the number of xylem bundles is not the primary factor for pith development, and while monocot roots do have an endodermis, it is not responsible for the pith's development.
